osmTags.inscription: EDMOND HALLEY 1656-1742
Jane Burden, Mrs William Morris, 1839-1914, Pre-Raphaelite muse and embroiderer was born in a dwelling in this passage 19th October 1839

In 1794
at the Star Inn near this site
The Oxfordshire Yeomanry
(Queen’s Own Oxfordshire Hussars)
was formed.

THIS ROSE GARDEN WAS GIVEN
IN HONOUR OF THE RESEARCH
WORKERS IN THIS UNIVERSITY WHO
DISCOVERED THE CLINICAL
IMPORTANCE OF PENICILLIN. [...]
Beneath this garden lies a medieval cemetery. [...]
This was the site of the Swindlestock Tavern 1250-1709

elements.name: Site of the Burning of the Oxford Martyrs

osmTags.inscription: Near this spot GEORGE NICHOLS RICHARD YAXLEY THOMAS BELSON HUMPHREY PRITCHARD were executed for their Catholic Faith 5 July 1589
Ivy Williams DCL (1877-1966), first woman to be called to the English Bar and to teach law at Oxford, lived here 1887-1904
Dedicated to the memory of Bruce Naylor (1920-2000) who loved his garden (but preferred his golf) donated by his daughter, Heather (Wadham 1976-79)
Christian Cole (d. 1885) / The first black African to be awarded an Oxford degree and to practise law in an English court was made a member of University College Oxford in 1877.

In a house on this site
between 1655 and 1668 lived
ROBERT BOYLE
Here he discovered BOYLE'S LAW
and made experiments with an
AIR PUMP designed by his assistant
ROBERT HOOKE
Inventor Scientist and Architect
who made a MICROSCOPE
[...]
ANDREW COMYN IRVINE 1902-1924 PERISHED NEAR THE SUMMIT OF MOUNT EVEREST JUNE 1924

Anthony à Wood
1632-1695
Antiquary
was born lived and died at Postmasters' Hall
James Sadler 1753~1828 First English Aeronaut who in a fire balloon made a successful ascent from near this place ~ 4th October 1784 to land near Woodeaton

THIS STONE MARKS THE PLACE
OF THE JEWISH CEMETERY
UNTIL 1290

Thomas Willis 1621-1675 Neurologist and Sedleian Professor of Natural Philosophy lived and worked here 1657-1667 Beam Hall formerly Biham Hall Named for Gilbert de Biham Ninth Chancellor of Oxford [Uni.] (1246) Owner of an earlier building on this site

IN THIS HOUSE WAS BORN Col. HENRY MARTEN GENTLEMAN COMMONER OF UNIVERSITY COLLEGE,
OXFORD MP FOR BERKSHIRE REPUBLICAN AND WIT.
1602-1680
In memory of Martin Wills/undergraduate at Magdalen College Oxford/1971 - 1974
SARAH COOPER 1848–1932 First made Oxford Marmalade here in 1874
This street known till 1300 as Great Jewry contained many houses of the Jews including the synagogue which lay to the north of Tom Tower 1931

eras.label: Mapped site · auto T1
eras.summary: Location and terrain only. OpenStreetMap has no mapped outline for this site.
eras.basis: Everything drawn is traced from OpenStreetMap ways (ODbL) and the Terrarium elevation tiles. Each element names its OSM way.
eras.conjecture: Walls and buildings without a sourced height are drawn as kerb-high plan lines, never as masses. Closed walls have no gates: none are mapped. The DEM is ~30 m source resolution: it cannot show terraces, ditches or scarps. Nothing historic is depicted.

notes: site: osm:relation/16470048 historic=citywalls 131 m from ledger point
site is a site relation of 23 parts and none of them outlines the whole site, so no outline is drawn; the scene is fitted to the parts (1008 x 538 m)
present-day buildings capped: kept the 30 nearest the outline centre of 998 mapped (trace size budget); the rest of the town is not drawn
roads capped: kept the 40 longest of 1190 mapped (trace size budget); minor lanes are not drawn
elements capped: kept the 380 nearest the ledger point of 455 mapped (trace size budget); the rest are not drawn
